title: Microsoft Teams: AI-generated meeting memory for knowledge retention
notes: 2026-11-16: taken offline; the grace for pages published before the check existed is off
summary: Hold: the retention command does not create an effective retention policy by itself, and the claim that meeting memory is included at no cost lacks published support. The briefing also omits the same-tenant access restriction and confuses the January rollout of administrator controls with memory generation four weeks later.

claims.claim: No administrator UI for inspecting or removing a meeting's generated memory is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting memory inspect remove generated memory Teams admin center Delete recap content. Opened the memory feature article and search results: administrator inspection/deletion uses PowerShell; Delete recap content is the organiser's meeting UI, not an admin-centre control.

claims.claim: Copilot for meetings and events is controlled through Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Copilot.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
Go to the Recording & transcription section and find the Copilot setting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy> -Copilot accepts Enabled, EnabledWithTranscript, EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn or Disabled.
claims.quote:
PowerShell setting value
Enabled
EnabledWithTranscript
EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn
Disabled
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Enabled
claims.fix: Keep the call supported by the cited management article, but note that https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/teams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy currently lists only Enabled and EnabledWithTranscript in its -Copilot parameter description; the management article documents all four values.

claims.claim: Retention policies are created through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.
Select New retention policy to start the Create retention policy configuration

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy alone is the automation equivalent for configuring retention of memory containers.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies). In addition, at least one location parameter must be defined to create a retention policy or retention label policy.
claims.fix: Replace the bare cmdlet with a scoped policy-and-rule sequence in Security & Compliance PowerShell: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy> -SharePointLocation <container-url>; New-RetentionComplianceRule -Name <rule> -Policy <policy> -RetentionDuration <days> -RetentionComplianceAction <action>. Explain that the action is Keep, Delete or KeepAndDelete and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-retentioncompliancerule?view=exchange-ps for the rule. Do not imply that creating an unscoped policy alone enforces retention.

claims.claim: Purview retention policies apply to memory files and can target their container URLs.
claims.quote:
Retention policies on memory files are managed in the Purview Data lifecycle management tool.
To target memory with a different policy, you can use the include or exclude settings to scope your search to your meeting memory container URLs.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The feature documentation states no additional licence for memory beyond its published prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting memory licensing pricing storage charges intelligent recap Teams Premium Copilot; "meeting memory" "included" "cost". Read the memory article and intelligent recap licensing: no separate memory licence stated.

claims.claim: Intelligent recap requires Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: You must assign a Teams Premium license or Microsoft Copilot license to your users.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/intelligent-recap-calls-meetings to sources for the recap licensing statement; preserve the separately stated Copilot-licensed-invitee prerequisite for memory generation.

claims.claim: No customer-visible storage charge for meeting memory is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting memory licensing pricing storage charges intelligent recap Teams Premium Copilot; "meeting memory" "included" "cost". Read the memory article's storage section and returned Microsoft documentation: no memory storage price or billing rule stated.

claims.claim: Meeting memory is included with Copilot and recap licensing, justifying cost none.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting memory licensing pricing storage charges intelligent recap Teams Premium Copilot; "meeting memory" "included" "cost". Read memory prerequisites/storage and intelligent recap licensing: no passage says memory is included at no additional cost.
claims.fix: Change cost to low for the documented administrative and communications work. Replace the rationale with 'Low. Compliance review, configuration and communication are the known costs; additional memory licensing and storage billing are not yet published.' Keep 'no additional licence stated' distinct from a promise of inclusion or no charge.

claims.claim: Turning off intelligent recap in meeting options prevents memory generation for that meeting.
claims.quote: Memory generation can be turned off for a specific meeting by turning off Intelligent Recap in the meeting options.

claims.claim: The meeting memory setting can be read back from the policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "meeting memory" "read" "policy" Teams PowerShell. Opened the memory article, full Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference and searched Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy: no passage identifies a meeting-memory readback property or procedure.
claims.fix: Remove 'and read back from the policy'. Retain the documented Teams admin center configuration route without implying an undocumented readback capability.

claims.where: Why it matters; rationale: impact; What's changing
claims.claim: Memory generation applies as soon as the January General Availability rollout arrives.
claims.quote:
The dates above reflect when admin controls become available.
Memory file generation will begin 4 weeks after the setting is released to your organization.
claims.fix: Keep January CY2027 as the roadmap target, but cite MC1429018 and state its actual sequencing: Targeted Release controls begin early January 2027 and complete mid-January 2027; Worldwide GA controls begin mid-January 2027 and complete late January 2027. Memory file generation begins four weeks after the setting reaches the organisation. Replace 'when GA arrives it will apply to every recapped meeting' and the impact rationale with 'memory generation begins four weeks after controls arrive, for eligible meetings with recap enabled and a Copilot-licensed invitee'.

claims.claim: The controls table covers the default-expiration setting administrators are instructed to configure.
claims.quote:
Set the Meeting memory meeting policy and the default expiration in the Teams admin center before GA reaches the tenant.
The controls rows cover generation, inspection/removal, Copilot, and Purview retention, but not the Teams default-expiration setting.
claims.fix: Add a separate 'Default expiration of meeting memory files' control row. The cited memory article documents the Teams admin center surface and configurable five-year default, but gives no exact navigation path; research that path and the automation equivalent before populating the row rather than inventing either.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot directly manage meeting memory containers through SharePoint Embedded APIs.
claims.quote: Meeting memory containers are fully managed in Microsoft Teams' services. Admins can't directly use SharePoint Embedded APIs to manage meeting memory containers.
